info.title: AnsibleForms API v2
info.description: API documentation for AnsibleForms v2 endpoints: authentication, system and health, users, groups and roles, settings, runners, credentials, secret stores, SSO providers, repositories, SSH and known hosts, notification channels, syslog servers, queries and expressions, jobs, stored jobs, schedules and planned runs, the forms designer, announcements, the disclaimer, backups, logs and the audit log.

get.summary: Get application settings
get.description: Returns application settings (URL, config source, language, theme, etc.). The mail settings are not settings since 7.6 : the mail goes through the mail channels (/notificationchannel).

config_yaml.description: The config.yaml content stored in the database (forms_yaml before 7.6)

put.description: Updates the settings row. Config CONTENT is deliberately not accepted here : it is written through PUT /settings/config, which validates it, honours the designer lock and the baseHash concurrency check, and writes a restore point. The mail_* fields of before 7.6 (deprecated, removed in 8) are ignored, with a warning in the log : the mail goes through the mail channels (/notificationchannel). They are never refused on their own account (a user limited to a settings section is not refused for them) ; a body of only mail_* fields changes nothing and answers 400 saying the mail settings moved to Connections > Notifications.

config_source.description: Where the active config is read from and written to

400.description: Missing required fields, or only mail_* fields (the mail settings moved to Connections > Notifications)

403.description: A field outside the caller's settings section (mail_* fields excepted), or one the config seed manages

get.summary: Get the active form configuration
get.description: Returns the active config.yaml content, read from the source set in config_source (database, use_for_config repository or local file). The returned baseHash is a sha256 fingerprint of that content; send it back on PUT to detect a concurrent change.

config_yaml.description: The active config.yaml content (empty string when there is none yet)

forms_yaml.description: The same content as config_yaml, under its name before 7.6 (deprecated, removed in 8)

baseHash.description: sha256 fingerprint of config_yaml, for optimistic concurrency on save

templated.description: The base config or a file a repository holds the roles, categories or constants in is a ytt template: the editors are read only

put.description: Validates the supplied yaml against the base schema and writes it to the active config source (database, use_for_config repository or local file). Refused while the designer holds the config lock, and to a user without the admin role when it changes the groups or users of the admin role.

config_yaml.description: The full config.yaml content (categories, roles, constants)

forms_yaml.description: Its name before 7.6 (deprecated, removed in 8) : taken when config_yaml is not sent

baseHash.description: Optional baseHash from GET /settings/config; when sent, the save is refused with 409 if the active config changed in the meantime

400.description: Missing config_yaml, invalid yaml, or config that fails the base schema validation

403.description: Only an admin can change who is an admin (the groups and users of the admin role), or take an option away from an admin

409.description: The active config changed elsewhere (stale baseHash), or the save would take admin, the sign-in or the settings away from the admin saving it

423.description: Configuration is locked by the designer

put.description: Loads the config.yaml (or the deprecated forms.yaml) file into the database, replacing the database copy. A restore point of that database copy is written to the backups first. Refused while the designer holds the config lock, and to a user without the admin role when the file changes the groups or users of the admin role or is a ytt template.

403.description: Only an admin can import a file that changes who is an admin, or whose roles cannot be read (a ytt template)

423.description: Configuration is locked by the designer

put.description: Writes the database config out to the config.yaml file (the repository copy when a use_for_config repository holds it). A restore point of the old file is written to the backups first. Refused when the database is not the active config source or holds no config, and while the designer holds the config lock.

400.description: The database is not the active config source, or there is no config in the database to export

423.description: Configuration is locked by the designer

get.summary: Get the active config mode
get.description: Returns whether the active form configuration lives in the database, resolved from the config_source setting with the ENABLE_CONFIG_IN_DATABASE environment default as fallback. Designer access is enough, so a designer without settings access can learn the mode.

configInDatabase.description: True when the active config is stored in the database

500.description: Failed to get the forms config

get.summary: List form names
get.description: Returns a sorted, de-duplicated flat list of the form names, for the form dropdown of schedules and stored jobs. A user of the settings or the schedules gets every form ; a user who may only store jobs (allowStoredJobs) gets the forms their roles open. Subforms are excluded because they cannot be launched standalone.

500.description: Failed to get the forms list

post.description: Deprecated since 7.6, removed in 8 : test a mail channel with POST /notificationchannel/{id}/test. Sends a test email with the mail server values sent. The settings hold no mail settings since 7.6 : a masked password, or no mail_server, stands for the mail settings the app sends with, so the test goes through the active mail channel (its own server and login) ; without one it answers 400 saying to add one under Connections > Notifications.

to.description: Email address to send test to

400.description: A masked password or no mail_server, and no active mail channel

get.summary: Get application log
get.description: Returns the last N lines of a day's application log file (today by default), unzipping a past day's .gz. A day without a file answers an empty log with the header X-Log-Missing: true.

parameters.name: lines
parameters.description: The last lines of the day's log to return: at most LOG_VIEW_LINES, and LOG_VIEW_LINES when left out (1000 by default)

parameters.name: date
parameters.description: The day, YYYY-MM-DD (a real calendar day, the server's local date); today when left out

200.description: Log content retrieved successfully; empty, with X-Log-Missing: true, when the day has no log file

X-Log-Missing.description: true when the day has no log file

X-Log-Date.description: The day read, YYYY-MM-DD: the server's today when no date was asked

schema.description: Last N lines of log file

400.description: The date is not a real day written as YYYY-MM-DD

get.summary: List the days that have a log file
get.description: The days with a main log file, plain or zipped (.gz), newest first. The errors log files are not counted.

get.summary: Download a day's log file
get.description: Downloads a day's log file (today by default): its .log, or a past day's zipped .log.gz as it is.

parameters.name: date
parameters.description: The day, YYYY-MM-DD (a real calendar day, the server's local date); today when left out

400.description: The date is not a real day written as YYYY-MM-DD

get.summary: List all repositories
get.description: Returns a list of all configured git repositories with masked passwords. For a user whose role option designAllForms, designAllPlaybooks or designAllWorkflows is off, the stored pull and push outputs leave out the lines naming files.

use_for_roles.description: The file of it giving controller_roles: (any name, any folder) holds the roles (config.yaml still read, deprecated). One repository at most

use_for_categories.description: The file of it giving controller_categories: (any name, any folder) holds the categories (config.yaml still read, deprecated). One repository at most

use_for_constants.description: The file of it giving controller_constants: (any name, any folder) holds the constants (config.yaml still read, deprecated). One repository at most

use_for_schedules.description: The controller_schedules: entries of its YAML files (any name, any folder) hold the schedules, read in after each pull. One repository at most : turning it on takes the app's recurring schedules (each written as an entry), turning it off keeps them in the app, unlinked

use_for_repositories.description: The controller_repositories: entries of its YAML files (any name, any folder) hold the other repositories, in the config seed format (never itself, never one holding repositories). One repository at most

use_for_credentials.description: The controller_credentials: entries of its YAML files (any name, any folder) hold the credentials, in the config seed format, secrets as ${ENV} references only. One repository at most : turning it on takes the app's credentials (written without their secrets), turning it off keeps them in the app, unlinked

use_for_databases.description: The controller_databases: entries of its YAML files (any name, any folder) hold the databases forms query, in the config seed format, each naming its credential of type database. One repository at most : turning it on takes the app's databases, turning it off keeps them in the app, unlinked

use_for_runners.description: The controller_runners: entries of its YAML files (any name, any folder) hold the runners, in the config seed format, naming their credential. One repository at most : turning it on takes the app's runners, turning it off keeps them in the app, unlinked

use_for_notifications.description: The controller_notifications: entries of its YAML files (any name, any folder) hold the notification channels, in the config seed format, naming their credentials, a webhook address as an ${ENV} reference only. One repository at most

use_for_sso.description: The controller_sso: entries of its YAML files (any name, any folder) hold the SSO providers, in the config seed format (oauth2 items), naming their credential, a client secret as an ${ENV} reference only. One repository at most

use_for_ldap.description: The controller_ldap: entries of its YAML files (any name, any folder) hold the LDAP directories (the seed's ldap section with the directory's name, position and domains), naming their credential. The main directory's entry cannot be removed while linked. One repository at most

use_for_syslog.description: The controller_syslog: entries of its YAML files (any name, any folder) hold the syslog servers, in the config seed format. One repository at most

use_for_chat_assistant.description: The controller_chat_assistant: map of one of its YAML files holds the chat assistant's switch (enable_chat, the ENABLE_CHAT environment setting) and its settings in the config seed format (its chat section), the api key as an ${ENV} reference only, naming its credential. One repository at most

use_for_mcp.description: The controller_mcp: map of one of its YAML files holds the MCP settings (Settings > Connections > MCP), keyed by their environment variable names in lower case. One repository at most

use_for_ssh.description: The controller_ssh: map of one of its YAML files holds the app's SSH key (an ${ENV} reference only) and its known hosts (Settings > Connections > SSH). One repository at most

use_for_disclaimer.description: The controller_disclaimer: entries of its YAML files (any name, any folder) hold the disclaimer versions (version, title, text, checkbox_label, enabled, ask_again). Acceptances are never in git. One repository at most

use_for_defaults.description: The controller_defaults: map of one of its YAML files holds what Settings > Appearance > Defaults saves: the theme and its colour, the forms view, the time zone, the date format and the language. One repository at most

use_for_logo.description: The controller_logo: map of one of its YAML files names the logo (Settings > Appearance > Logo), an image file of the repository relative to that file, read and written as binary. One repository at most

use_for_icon.description: The controller_icon: map of one of its YAML files names the website icon (Settings > Appearance > Icon), an image file of the repository relative to that file, read and written as binary. One repository at most

use_for_name.description: The controller_name: map of one of its YAML files holds the app name (Settings > Appearance > Name). One repository at most

use_for_links.description: The controller_links: map of one of its YAML files holds the header links and the Designer link (Settings > Appearance > Links). One repository at most

use_for_labels.description: The controller_labels: entries of its YAML files (any name, any folder) hold the labels beside the logo, in the config seed format, with their position. One repository at most

use_for_announcements.description: The controller_announcements: entries of its YAML files (any name, any folder) hold the announcements, named, with their schedule and switch. One repository at most

use_for_general.description: The controller_general: map of one of its YAML files holds the System > General settings by their environment variable names in lower case (those that page changes), secrets as ${ENV} references only, applied as that page saves them. One repository at most

post.summary: Relaunch job by ID, as it ran or with some fields changed
post.description: Without a body the job is replayed with the extravars it ran with. With a body holding `values`, the values the job was launched with are taken, `values` is laid over them, and the result goes through the form engine again - resolved, validated and the extravars built by the server - as a new launch by the caller. Uploads of the original are reused. Without a body, or for a form under launch validation 'enforce', see the Launch validation page : a relaunch that goes through the check is refused (400) for a password field the form shows, since passwords are never stored with the field values ; one its dependencies hide does not count. Only for the job's owner, an admin or a user who sees every job. Needs the form to allow relaunch and the allowJobRelaunch role option. A job launched from a stored job passes it on : the new job names it (storedJob) and its last_used_at is set, when the caller may read that stored job (as GET /stored-jobs/{id}) ; one deleted since is skipped.

Refused (400) for a job without failed hosts, a workflow or multistep job, and a Jenkins, Semaphore or Rundeck job. The answer lists them as failedHosts.

Refused (400) for a job that did not fail, a multistep job, an AWX or AAP workflow job, a job from before 7.7.0 and a workflow that changed since. Not together with failedHostsOnly.

get.summary: List stored jobs, filter by form, or get one by name
get.description: Needs the allowStoredJobs role option (403 otherwise). By name only the caller's own are searched; by form_name the caller's own and, with the allowStoredJobsViewAll role option, the ones other users shared (visibility shared) of a form the caller may open that does not set allowStoredJobSharing: false; another user's comes without the values of its password fields, in list and yaml rows too. The full list shows everyone's to a user with the settings permission, otherwise only the caller's own.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Return the caller's stored job with this name (data is null when none)

parameters.name: form_name
parameters.description: Only the stored jobs of this form: the caller's own, and the ones shared with them

200.description: Stored job list or single stored job, each with its created_at, expires_at and last_used_at (when a job was last launched from it, null until then)

post.description: Needs the allowStoredJobs role option (403 otherwise). The owner is the calling user. A shared one (visibility shared) needs the allowStoredJobsShare role option and a form that does not set allowStoredJobSharing: false.

201.description: Stored job created; data is { id }

400.description: Missing required field, a value too long, a visibility other than private or shared, or unused_days not allowed (see StoredJob)

403.description: No allowStoredJobs, or sharing without allowStoredJobsShare or on a form that does not allow it

409.description: The caller already has a stored job with this name for this form

get.summary: Get a stored job by ID
get.description: Needs the allowStoredJobs role option (403 otherwise). A user without the settings permission only reaches their own stored jobs, and the ones shared with them (see the list by form_name). One shared by another user comes without the values of its password fields, in list and yaml rows too.

200.description: Stored job, with its created_at, expires_at and last_used_at (when a job was last launched from it, null until then)

403.description: No allowStoredJobs, or another user's stored job

put.summary: Update a stored job by ID
put.description: Needs the allowStoredJobs role option (403 otherwise). A user without the settings permission only reaches their own stored jobs ; one shared with them is not theirs to change. A body without writable fields changes nothing. Sharing it (visibility shared) needs the allowStoredJobsShare role option and a form that allows it. unused_days follows the rule of the StoredJob schema.

400.description: A visibility other than private or shared, or unused_days not allowed (see StoredJob)

403.description: No allowStoredJobs, or another user's stored job

409.description: Name already used for this form

delete.summary: Delete a stored job by ID
delete.description: Needs the allowStoredJobs role option (403 otherwise). A user without the settings permission only reaches their own stored jobs.

403.description: No allowStoredJobs, or another user's stored job

post.description: A runner's one registration call, before an inbound runner listens (so the app knows the address to dial); an outbound runner registers when it dials. No user signs in: the runner's own token, or a join token, is the proof. Limited per address, as the sign-in is.

parameters.name: Authorization
parameters.description: Bearer and the runner's token (RTE_TOKEN), at least 16 characters

parameters.name: X-AF-RTE-Join
parameters.description: A join token, for a runner the app does not know yet

mode.description: Inbound: the app dials the runner ; outbound: the runner dials the app

url.description: An inbound runner's address, which the app dials (RTE_URL)

cert.description: An inbound runner's certificate (PEM), only with an https address

pending.description: Waits for an admin's approval under Connections > Runners

400.description: A name, address or certificate that is missing or not valid

401.description: The token is missing, too short or not the runner's, or the join token is unknown, revoked, expired or used up

409.description: The name is another type of runner, the runner is managed by the config seed, or it waits for approval

429.description: Too many attempts from this address

bearerAuth.description: JWT Bearer token. Authenticate via /auth/login, then use 'Authorize' here.

metricsToken.description: The value of the METRICS_TOKEN environment variable, for /metrics only.

Runner.description: Where a job runs. type rte : a runtime environment container (AF_ROLE=rte) for playbooks. type awx : AWX / Ansible Automation Platform / Ascender for templates. type semaphore : Semaphore UI for templates, in one project. type rundeck : Rundeck jobs, in one project. type jenkins : Jenkins jobs, signed in with a user and its API token, in a folder if any.

token.description: rte : its RTE_TOKEN. awx : an API token (or use_credentials). semaphore : an API token of a Semaphore user. rundeck : a user's API token. jenkins : the API token of the user in username

use_credentials.description: awx : sign in with username and password instead of a token

is_default.description: Used by playbook forms that name no runner

project.description: semaphore : the id of the project its templates are in. rundeck : the name of the project its jobs are in. jenkins : the folder its jobs are in (ops, or ops/web), none for the top

flavour.description: awx : which product it is, Ansible Automation Platform or Ascender ; none is AWX. Its uri may carry its API path (https://aap.example.com/api/controller/v2)

node_id.description: rte : the node of a runner that registered itself (RTE_REGISTER) ; empty when added by hand or by the config seed

repository.description: The runners repository it comes from ; empty for one kept in the app only. Written by the repository's pull, never by a request

repo_file.description: The file its entry is in, in that repository (any name, any folder : runners.yaml)

state.description: Only on a runner that registered itself : automatic while it writes its heartbeat, unresponsive once it stopped (removed by the worker after 10 minutes)

SyslogServer.description: A syslog server the server log and the audit entries are sent to.

repository.description: The repository it comes from (Settings > Connections > Repositories) ; empty for one kept in the app only. Written by the repository's pull, never by a request

repo_file.description: The file its entry is in, in that repository (any name, any folder : syslog.yaml)

host.description: Required unless the protocol is unix or unix-connect

path.description: The socket, for unix and unix-connect

level.description: The lowest level of the server log it gets; audit entries are always sent

source.description: The host the lines say they come from

NotificationChannel.description: A notification channel. Which fields are used depends on the type.

repository.description: The repository it comes from (Settings > Connections > Repositories) ; empty for one kept in the app only. Written by the repository's pull, never by a request

repo_file.description: The file its entry is in, in that repository (any name, any folder : notifications.yaml)

is_active.description: mail: the one the app sends its mail with

server.description: mail: read, the server of its smtp credential. Written, deprecated since 7.3 : used only while the credential has no host

port.description: mail: as server, the credential's port

secure.description: mail: as server, the credential's TLS

credential.description: mail: an smtp credential (the server and the login), or an entraid one to send through Microsoft 365 as from_address

send_through.description: mail with an entraid credential: Microsoft Graph, or SMTP with OAuth2 (smtp.office365.com:587)

webhook_url.description: slack, teams: the webhook address, a secret (masked when read)

api_url.description: telegram: the Bot API address, empty for api.telegram.org

token_credential.description: telegram: an api credential whose password is the bot token; webhook: an api credential whose password is the bearer token

headers.description: webhook: extra headers, a JSON object

repository.description: The repository it comes from (Settings > Connections > Repositories) ; empty for one kept in the app only. Written by the repository's pull, never by a request

repo_file.description: The file its entry is in, in that repository (any name, any folder : ldap.yaml)

name.description: letters, digits, - and _ ; 'default' keeps its members' short names (ldap/<group>, the bare username), any other's are ldap/<name>/<group> and <name>/<user>

position.description: the order a bare username is looked up in, the lowest first

domains.description: sign-in domains, comma separated : user@domain goes straight to this directory

server.description: one or more servers, comma separated, each host, host:port or ldap(s)://host:port ; the next one is tried when one cannot be reached. Read : its ldap credential's servers (host). Written : deprecated since 7.3, used only while the credential has none ; port, enable_tls, ignore_certs, cert and ca_bundle the same

credential.description: a credential of Connections > Credentials to bind with instead of bind_user_dn and bind_user_pw

SecretStore.description: A secret store. Which fields are used depends on the type.

repository.description: The repository it comes from (Settings > Connections > Repositories) ; empty for one kept in the app only. Written by the repository's pull, never by a request

repo_file.description: The file its entry is in, in that repository (any name, any folder : secret_stores.yaml)

client_cert.description: A cyberark credential's client certificate (PEM) ; an entraid one's certificate, used instead of its client secret to send mail through Microsoft 365

client_key.description: The private key (PEM, no passphrase) of client_cert, stored encrypted and masked when read

cache_ttl_seconds.description: 0 reads the secret on every use

extra.description: JSON object with options of the store type

repository.description: The databases repository it comes from (Settings > Connections > Repositories) ; empty for one kept in the app only. Written by the repository's pull, never by a request

repo_file.description: The file its entry is in, in that repository (any name, any folder : databases.yaml)

name.description: The name a field's dbConfig gives

credential.description: The credential of type database it connects with: its engine, server, database and login

used_by_count.description: In the list: the forms naming it, or its credential, in a field's dbConfig

managed.description: Declared by the config seed: read only

user.description: Database user (leave empty when using a secret store).

password.description: Database password (leave empty when using a secret store).

host.description: Where it connects : an ssh or a database one's host, an smtp one's mail server, an ldap one's directory servers in failover order (required for smtp and ldap).

secure.description: Use a secure connection (an smtp or an ldap one : TLS).

ignore_certs.description: An ldap credential : the servers' certificates not checked

ca_bundle.description: An ldap credential : the CA bundle its servers' certificates are checked against (its client certificate is client_cert)

used_by_count.description: In the list : how many secret stores, notification channels, repositories, LDAP directories, SSO providers and chat settings use it

credential_type.description: What the credential is for ; is_database follows it

client_key.description: A cyberark credential's client key, or an ssh credential's private key (PEM or OpenSSH). Stored encrypted, always returned masked ; the mask or an empty value sent back keeps it, null removes it

key_passphrase.description: The passphrase of an ssh credential's private key. Stored encrypted, always returned masked ; the mask or an empty value sent back keeps it, null removes it

tenant_id.description: An entraid credential's tenant (its user is the client ID, its password the client secret)

issuer.description: An oidc credential's issuer, the provider's address (its user is the client ID, its password the client secret)

redirect_uri.description: An entraid or oidc credential's redirect URL, as registered with its client. Empty : the app's URL setting and the type's callback path (/api/v2/auth/entraid/callback, /api/v2/auth/oidc/callback)

secret_store.description: Name of the secret store user and password are read from.

secret_ref.description: Where the secret lives in the store, e.g. a Vault path.

repository.description: The credentials repository it comes from (Settings > Connections > Repositories) ; empty for one kept in the app only. Written by the repository's pull, never by a request

repo_file.description: The file its entry is in, in that repository (any name, any folder : credentials.yaml)

vault_path.description: Deprecated since 7, removed in 8 : the same as secret_store 'vault' with this secret_ref.

formName.description: Name of the form to launch.

payload.description: The same as extravars, the word a Rundeck job uses ; when both are sent, extravars wins.

job_type.description: Type of job (e.g., ansible, awx, multistep).

storedJobId.description: The stored job the values came from (the form opened with ?storedJob=<id>) : its last_used_at is set to now, and the job names it (storedJob in GET /job/{id}). Ignored unless the caller may read it (as GET /stored-jobs/{id}) and it is of this form.

OAuth2Provider.description: OAuth2 provider configuration object (Azure AD, OIDC, etc.).

repository.description: The repository it comes from (Settings > Connections > Repositories) ; empty for one kept in the app only. Written by the repository's pull, never by a request

repo_file.description: The file its entry is in, in that repository (any name, any folder : sso.yaml)

id.description: Unique identifier for the OAuth2 provider.

issuer.description: OIDC issuer URL. Deprecated since 7.3 : the issuer of its oidc credential, used only while it has no credential.

tenant_id.description: Entra ID tenant ID. Deprecated since 7.3 : the tenant of its entraid credential, used only while it has no credential.

client_id.description: OAuth2 client ID (required unless credential is set).

client_secret.description: OAuth2 client secret (required unless credential is set). Use '**********' to preserve existing secret when updating.

credential.description: A credential of Connections > Credentials to sign in as instead: its user is the client ID, its password the client secret.

enable.description: Enable this provider (1 = enabled, 0 = disabled). Only one provider of each type can be enabled.

redirect_uri.description: OAuth2 redirect URI. Deprecated since 7.3 : the redirect URL of its credential, used only while the credential has none.

userinfo_url.description: User info URL (optional, auto-discovered for OIDC).

expiryDays.description: Lifetime in days, at most API_TOKEN_MAX_DAYS; 'never' needs extendedTokenExpiration

blocked.description: true blocks the sign-in, false allows it

description.description: Who the user is or what the account is for

path.description: File path relative to the kind's folder (prefixed with the repository name when there are several roots).

FormsConfigDocument.description: The forms configuration (categories, roles, constants, forms) as an object; a non-admin may not change the roles.

message.description: the text shown (trimmed, cut at 500 characters)

start_at.description: when it starts showing; none : at once

end_at.description: when it stops showing (then it is deleted); after start_at and in the future

description.description: What it is for, in a few words

one_time_run.description: Run once, at this moment, instead of on a cron or a rrule: ISO 8601 with its offset or Z (a schedules repository's refuses one without a zone, 400); null takes it off. Exactly one of one_time_run, cron and rrule is kept

rrule.description: An iCal rrule, on one line, instead of a cron (validated, 400 if refused)

run_at.description: Deprecated since 7.8.0, removed in 8: the moment before one_time_run held it (with one_time_run true, or alone). Read as one_time_run

extra_vars.description: Extra vars as a YAML/JSON string

enabled.description: Off: the cron or one-time run does not fire (launch still works)

ends.description: How a schedule timed by a cron or a rrule ends: never (the default), on a date (end_at) or after a number of runs (end_count). Ignored for a one-time run. A rrule's own UNTIL or COUNT still applies

end_at.description: Required with ends date: the moment it ends at, ISO 8601 with its offset or Z (400 when missing or no time). A schedule whose end_at passed never launches

end_count.description: Required with ends count: the runs it ends after, at least 1 (400 otherwise). Counted in run_count, the jobs it started in all

end_action.description: What its end does: turns it off (the default) or removes it. A schedules repository's schedule is only ever turned off, its file manages it

remove_after_run.description: A one-time run: removed after it started its job (the default), else turned off and kept with its outcome. A planned job is always removed

planned.description: Create only: plan a one-time run as the calling user (Run later) instead of an admin-level schedule

raw_form_data.description: Create of a planned run only: the raw field values (object or JSON string), checked by launch validation

stored_job_id.description: Create of a planned run only: the stored job the values came from. Kept when the caller may read it (as GET /stored-jobs/{id}) and it is of this form; its last_used_at is set when the run fires. Ignored for a schedule

Schedule.description: Fields owner, state, output, last_run and queue_id are ignored on write.

name.description: Name, unique per user and form

form_data.description: The form values as a JSON string

visibility.description: private (default): only the owner. shared: also the users with the allowStoredJobsViewAll role option, who can load it but not change it

unused_days.description: Removed once no job was launched from it for this many days, counted from its last_used_at (or its created_at, never used). null (or left out) follows STORED_JOB_UNUSED_DAYS. While that setting is above 0 it must be from 1 to the setting (400 otherwise) ; with the setting 0 any whole number of at least 1. null (or left out) always follows the setting, which still removes it. The days that count are the shorter of the two ; expires_at keeps working, whichever comes first removes it

last_used_at.description: When a job was last launched from it (POST /job with its storedJobId, the MCP launch_job, a planned run from it when it fires, or a relaunch of a job launched from it) ; null until then. Set by the server only

StoredJob.description: Only these fields are written; id, username (always the caller), created_at and last_used_at are ignored. name, form_name and form_data are required on create.
